title: The AI Bailout Could Be Baked Into the AI Bubble
excerpt: Instead of passing through bankruptcy, insolvent life insurers have all their liabilities—in particular the policyholder claims—paid for by state guaranty funds.
content_html:
A hedge fund worth $45 billion at its height sold nearly its entire stock portfolio to Citadel Securities last week. As recently as a month ago, the fund was up 439 percent on the year, according to an investor letter from its founder, 24-year-old former OpenAI employee Leopold Aschenbrenner. But its portfolio, aggressively invested in companies tied to the artificial intelligence industry, dropped 67 percent in July.

Hilariously, the fund was called Situational Awareness.

Last week, the tech-heavy Nasdaq saw its second correction of the year, named for a drop of at least 10 percent from its peak. SpaceX has lost the equivalent of the entire value of Tesla since its post-IPO high in June, and it’s still dropping. For whatever reason—the rise of cheaper and more flexible Chinese AI models, the recognition that U.S. AI companies simply aren’t generating enough revenue to justify skyrocketing capital expenditures, the general economic drag from Trump’s tariffs and wars, or the increasingly operatic financial maneuvers to keep the wheels moving—the shine is way off the AI rose for investors.

More from David Dayen

The problem is that the industry is bound so tightly with the stock market that a change in feeling from AI investors could be all it takes to generate a market-wide crash, as we’re seeing to some degree. In other words, if AI is propping up the economy, who is propping up AI?

The answer, extrapolating from a fascinating new paper about private credit and the life insurance industry, could be the U.S. taxpayer.

Private credit is private equity’s $3 trillion financing arm. They make largely unregulated, relatively high-risk, relatively complex and opaque loans, mostly to their own portfolio companies. Private credit is entangled, maybe more than the rest of Wall Street, in AI mania. For example, in the mid-2010s private equity bought up hundreds of software-as-a-service providers, and its private credit affiliates made thousands of loans to them, only to see these portfolio companies buckle recently as AI replicated their tasks.

A deeper intertwining can be seen with all the loans private credit companies have made to build AI data centers across the country. As delays in construction grow—some 530 local jurisdictions and counting have passed data center restrictions or bans—and as the AI industry seems less of a solid bet, these loans could go into mass default. Higher interest rates, thanks to the disastrous war in Iran keeping inflation high, have also become a private credit stress point. As a result, redemption requests from nervous investors continue to grow.

Yet none of this has stopped the private credit giants, even as share prices have crumbled. One of the biggest, KKR, recently reported record earnings. What explains this disconnect? It could be linked to a separate business line that has given many private equity firms what consulting giant McKinsey has described as “permanent capital.”

Private equity today owns at least $1.5 trillion in assets in life insurance companies. Apollo bought Athene in 2022; KKR got Global Atlantic a couple of years earlier. As explained in a research paper by Andrew Granato, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin, and Pranjal Drall, a Ph.D. candidate at Yale, these life insurers have mounds of available capital from policyholder payments that don’t need to be paid out until the end of their lives. Private equity firms have plowed this capital into risky private credit loans that could weaken the structure of the life insurer. But if the insurer goes insolvent, the private equity firm won’t have to pay; you will.

That’s because instead of passing through bankruptcy, insolvent life insurers have all their liabilities—in particular the policyholder claims—paid for by state guaranty funds. After the fact, those funds impose assessments on surviving life insurers in a particular state. The apparent idea was to protect life insurance beneficiaries, and to pay for it through fees on the industry as a whole. But the choice of policy design means the successful companies pay for the bad behavior of the insolvent ones. And it gets worse in most of the country: In 44 states, life insurers can take a tax credit for that assessment and get paid back 100 percent over a period of time.

In other words, the risks being taken by private credit companies ultimately transfer to state taxpayers. It’s a familiar story of privatizing the profits and socializing the risks. Private equity scented that opportunity a long way off.

“These incentives for insurers to take on this amount of risk have existed for a long time,” said Granato in an interview. “But private equity’s entry into the business marks this really sharp shift in the asset management profiles of their balance sheets.” Private equity is capitalizing on the bailout guarantee scheme by playing very close to the edge, and threatening the entire economy alongside it.

Private equity profits greatly from its relationship with life insurers. Granato and Drall find that after a life insurance company is bought by a private equity firm, it typically cuts its internal investment team in half, and drops that team entirely in one-third of the cases. Instead, the life insurer pays an affiliate of the private equity firm to invest for them. Numerous other fees for accounting, data systems, and other services funnel up to the private equity parent.

Life insurance capital is invariably used to purchase underperforming private credit loans, rather than the boring mix of Treasurys and corporate bonds that usually make up the investments. “In 2024, 49.5 percent of new private equity-owned insurers’ investment was in privately-placed instruments,” Granato and Prall write. For nonaffiliated life insurers, that number was around 14 percent.

The captive life insurer, in other words, is leaking out more money to its private equity owner and taking much higher risk on its balance sheet. No policyholder really knows this is happening and isn’t used to checking the holdings of its life insurer. “The consumers might actually get a better price,” said Drall, noting that higher risk often comes with a higher return, at least initially. “You might imagine that consumers are even happy to buy Athene.”

The threat, of course, is that all these bad private credit loans are being dumped into a part of the system that is not being closely monitored, by customers or regulators.

Insurance products are regulated at the state level by overmatched and often captured insurance commissioners. They don’t have the expertise to understand the complex loans coming into the life insurer, and they don’t really want to know anyway. “What ends up happening is that state regulators are actually competing with each other to loosen life insurance regulation,” Granato said. In addition, private equity firms pay lenient rating agencies to give their sketchy loans a clean bill of health, which is quickly accepted by the insurance commissioner.

Granato and Drall estimate in their paper that private credit loan default rates above 15 percent could generate insolvency. The subscription-based Capitol Forum noted last week that KKR and Apollo’s three life insurers have just a tiny amount of room in its hardest-to-value assets to absorb losses. “There is an expectation, even by the regulators, that the music is going to stop,” one insurance actuary told the publication.

A major life insurer insolvency is uncharted territory. “We’ve been very lucky, I think, that there’s been no major insurer insolvencies that have had to be mediated through the guaranty fund system, because there’s kind of an open question as to if this is even logistically possible to do,” Granato said. He noted that AIG, the insurer that collapsed after the 2008 crisis, was saved by quick action by the Fed and later Congress. “If AIG had been allowed to go under and then we would have had to manage 50 simultaneous AIG insolvencies across every state, in the middle of the financial crisis?” he asked. “You can imagine what a nightmare that would be.”

It’s unclear to Granato and Drall how we even ended up with this state guaranty/tax credit system; the historical literature shows shockingly little debate. But while protecting policyholders from ruin if their insurers made bad investments is certainly a good goal, doing it with after-the-fact assessments that get paid out by state tax credits is just a backdoor bailout. And it isn’t a particularly good disciplinary tool for the industry, as the insolvent insurer is off the hook from paying anything.

“It makes sense if you had a good supervisory regime,” Drall said. But the weak regime means that risk-taking is incentivized, especially if a private equity fund can extract from the insurer along the way and be held harmless afterward.

And when you bring in the fact that private credit is making all these data center loans, this risk-taking is dangerously concentrated. “Based on the fact that private equity firms specialize in this kind of lending, just the whole financial system is more and more aligned on that kind of activity,” said Drall. “And the more you do that, you know, AI better work out to sort of support the ecosystem.”

Granato and Drall offer several reform proposals, mostly around making risks more transparent by reforming the valuation of private credit (including penalizing the companies for their opacity and complexity) and scrutinizing the rating agencies that claim the assets are safe. Internal transactions between private credit and the life insurer should have enhanced review, they argue, and the fees private equity takes out of the insurer should be identified in risk review.

But their big ask is to change how guaranty funds assess the industry after the fact instead of before, and how the tax credits effectively put the risk on taxpayers. An alternative would be assessing all companies before the fact, and assessing their corporate parents—including the private equity firms. “The core problem is having the ex post design in the first place, rather than funding it the way federal deposit insurance does it,” Granato said.

Otherwise, there’s this whole super-important industry that’s precariously tied to the AI bubble, and if the bet fails, we’d all be stuck holding the bag.

sentences.zh: 阿波罗于 2022 年收购了雅典娜； KKR 几年前收购了 Global Atlantic。

sentences.en: As explained in a research paper by Andrew Granato, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin, and Pranjal Drall, a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 正如德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校助理教授 Andrew Granato 和博士 Pranjal Drall 在一篇研究论文中所解释的那样。

sentences.en: candidate at Yale, these life insurers have mounds of available capital from policyholder payments that don’t need to be paid out until the end of their lives.
sentences.zh: 耶鲁大学的候选人表示，这些人寿保险公司拥有大量来自保单持有人付款的可用资本，这些资本在他们生命结束之前都不需要支付。

sentences.en: Private equity firms have plowed this capital into risky private credit loans that could weaken the structure of the life insurer.
sentences.zh: 私募股权公司已将这些资金投入高风险的私人信贷贷款，这可能会削弱寿险公司的结构。

sentences.en: But if the insurer goes insolvent, the private equity firm won’t have to pay; you will.
sentences.zh: 但如果保险公司资不抵债，私募股权公司就不必支付；你会。

blocks.html_en: That’s because instead of passing through bankruptcy, insolvent life insurers have all their liabilities—in particular the policyholder claims—paid for by state guaranty funds. After the fact, those funds impose assessments on surviving life insurers in a particular state. The apparent idea was to protect life insurance beneficiaries, and to pay for it through fees on the industry as a whole. But the choice of policy design means the successful companies pay for the bad behavior of the insolvent ones. And it gets worse in most of the country: In 44 states, life insurers can take a tax credit for that assessment and get paid back 100 percent over a period of time.

sentences.en: That’s because instead of passing through bankruptcy, insolvent life insurers have all their liabilities—in particular the policyholder claims—paid for by state guaranty funds.
sentences.zh: 这是因为，资不抵债的人寿保险公司不会破产，而是由国家担保基金支付其所有负债，特别是保单持有人的索赔。

sentences.en: After the fact, those funds impose assessments on surviving life insurers in a particular state.
sentences.zh: 事后，这些基金会对特定州幸存的人寿保险公司进行评估。

sentences.en: The apparent idea was to protect life insurance beneficiaries, and to pay for it through fees on the industry as a whole.
sentences.zh: 明显的想法是保护人寿保险受益人，并通过整个行业的费用来支付费用。

sentences.en: But the choice of policy design means the successful companies pay for the bad behavior of the insolvent ones.
sentences.zh: 但政策设计的选择意味着成功的公司要为无力偿债的公司的不良行为付出代价。

sentences.en: And it gets worse in most of the country: In 44 states, life insurers can take a tax credit for that assessment and get paid back 100 percent over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 在美国大部分地区，情况变得更糟：在 44 个州，人寿保险公司可以获得该评估的税收抵免，并在一段时间内获得 100% 的偿还。

blocks.html_en: In other words, the risks being taken by private credit companies ultimately transfer to state taxpayers. It’s a familiar story of privatizing the profits and socializing the risks. Private equity scented that opportunity a long way off.

sentences.en: In other words, the risks being taken by private credit companies ultimately transfer to state taxpayers.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，私人信贷公司承担的风险最终转移给了国家纳税人。

sentences.en: It’s a familiar story of privatizing the profits and socializing the risks.
sentences.zh: 这是一个熟悉的利润私有化和风险社会化的故事。

sentences.en: Private equity scented that opportunity a long way off.
sentences.zh: 私募股权公司早就嗅到了这个机会。

blocks.html_en: “These incentives for insurers to take on this amount of risk have existed for a long time,” said Granato in an interview. “But private equity’s entry into the business marks this really sharp shift in the asset management profiles of their balance sheets.” Private equity is capitalizing on the bailout guarantee scheme by playing very close to the edge, and threatening the entire economy alongside it.

sentences.en: “These incentives for insurers to take on this amount of risk have existed for a long time,” said Granato in an interview.
sentences.zh: “这些鼓励保险公司承担如此大风险的激励措施已经存在很长时间了，”格拉纳托在接受采访时表示。

sentences.en: “But private equity’s entry into the business marks this really sharp shift in the asset management profiles of their balance sheets.”
sentences.zh: “但私募股权进入该业务标志着其资产负债表的资产管理状况发生了真正的急剧转变。”

sentences.en: Private equity is capitalizing on the bailout guarantee scheme by playing very close to the edge, and threatening the entire economy alongside it.
sentences.zh: 私募股权正在利用救助担保计划，在非常接近边缘的情况下发挥作用，并威胁到整个经济。

blocks.html_en: Private equity profits greatly from its relationship with life insurers. Granato and Drall find that after a life insurance company is bought by a private equity firm, it typically cuts its internal investment team in half, and drops that team entirely in one-third of the cases. Instead, the life insurer pays an affiliate of the private equity firm to invest for them. Numerous other fees for accounting, data systems, and other services funnel up to the private equity parent.

sentences.en: Private equity profits greatly from its relationship with life insurers.
sentences.zh: 私募股权公司从其与人寿保险公司的关系中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: Granato and Drall find that after a life insurance company is bought by a private equity firm, it typically cuts its internal investment team in half, and drops that team entirely in one-third of the cases.
sentences.zh: 格拉纳托和德拉尔发现，一家人寿保险公司被私募股权公司收购后，通常会将其内部投资团队削减一半，并在三分之一的情况下完全放弃该团队。

sentences.en: Instead, the life insurer pays an affiliate of the private equity firm to invest for them.
sentences.zh: 相反，人寿保险公司向私募股权公司的附属公司付费，让其为其投资。

sentences.en: Numerous other fees for accounting, data systems, and other services funnel up to the private equity parent.
sentences.zh: 会计、数据系统和其他服务的许多其他费用都集中到私募股权母公司身上。

blocks.html_en: Life insurance capital is invariably used to purchase underperforming private credit loans, rather than the boring mix of Treasurys and corporate bonds that usually make up the investments. “In 2024, 49.5 percent of new private equity-owned insurers’ investment was in privately-placed instruments,” Granato and Prall write. For nonaffiliated life insurers, that number was around 14 percent.

sentences.en: Life insurance capital is invariably used to purchase underperforming private credit loans, rather than the boring mix of Treasurys and corporate bonds that usually make up the investments.
sentences.zh: 人寿保险资本总是用于购买表现不佳的私人信贷贷款，而不是通常构成投资的国债和公司债券的无聊组合。

sentences.en: “In 2024, 49.5 percent of new private equity-owned insurers’ investment was in privately-placed instruments,” Granato and Prall write.
sentences.zh: Granato 和 Prall 写道：“到 2024 年，新成立的私募股权保险公司的投资中有 49.5% 投资于私募工具。”

sentences.en: For nonaffiliated life insurers, that number was around 14 percent.
sentences.zh: 对于非附属人寿保险公司来说，这个数字约为 14%。

blocks.html_en: The captive life insurer, in other words, is leaking out more money to its private equity owner and taking much higher risk on its balance sheet. No policyholder really knows this is happening and isn’t used to checking the holdings of its life insurer. “The consumers might actually get a better price,” said Drall, noting that higher risk often comes with a higher return, at least initially. “You might imagine that consumers are even happy to buy Athene.”

sentences.en: The captive life insurer, in other words, is leaking out more money to its private equity owner and taking much higher risk on its balance sheet.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，自保人寿保险公司正在向其私募股权所有者泄露更多资金，并在其资产负债表上承担更高的风险。

sentences.en: No policyholder really knows this is happening and isn’t used to checking the holdings of its life insurer.
sentences.zh: 没有保单持有人真正知道这种情况正在发生，也不习惯检查其人寿保险公司的资产。

sentences.en: “The consumers might actually get a better price,” said Drall, noting that higher risk often comes with a higher return, at least initially.
sentences.zh: 德拉尔表示：“消费者实际上可能会得到更好的价格。”他指出，较高的风险往往伴随着较高的回报，至少在最初是这样。

sentences.en: “You might imagine that consumers are even happy to buy Athene.”
sentences.zh: “你可能会想象消费者甚至很乐意购买 Athene。”

blocks.html_en: The threat, of course, is that all these bad private credit loans are being dumped into a part of the system that is not being closely monitored, by customers or regulators.

sentences.en: The threat, of course, is that all these bad private credit loans are being dumped into a part of the system that is not being closely monitored, by customers or regulators.
sentences.zh: 当然，威胁在于所有这些不良私人信用贷款都被转入系统中不受客户或监管机构密切监控的部分。

blocks.html_en: Insurance products are regulated at the state level by overmatched and often captured insurance commissioners. They don’t have the expertise to understand the complex loans coming into the life insurer, and they don’t really want to know anyway. “What ends up happening is that state regulators are actually competing with each other to loosen life insurance regulation,” Granato said. In addition, private equity firms pay lenient rating agencies to give their sketchy loans a clean bill of health, which is quickly accepted by the insurance commissioner.

sentences.en: Insurance products are regulated at the state level by overmatched and often captured insurance commissioners.
sentences.zh: 保险产品在州一级由实力雄厚且经常被俘虏的保险专员进行监管。

sentences.en: They don’t have the expertise to understand the complex loans coming into the life insurer, and they don’t really want to know anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们没有专业知识来理解人寿保险公司收到的复杂贷款，而且他们也不想知道。

sentences.en: “What ends up happening is that state regulators are actually competing with each other to loosen life insurance regulation,” Granato said.
sentences.zh: “最终发生的情况是，各州监管机构实际上正在相互竞争，以放松人寿保险监管，”格拉纳托说。

sentences.en: In addition, private equity firms pay lenient rating agencies to give their sketchy loans a clean bill of health, which is quickly accepted by the insurance commissioner.
sentences.zh: 此外，私募股权公司还向宽松的评级机构支付费用，让其不良贷款获得良好的健康证明，这一点很快就得到了保险专员的认可。

blocks.html_en: Granato and Drall estimate in their paper that private credit loan default rates above 15 percent could generate insolvency. The subscription-based Capitol Forum noted last week that KKR and Apollo’s three life insurers have just a tiny amount of room in its hardest-to-value assets to absorb losses. “There is an expectation, even by the regulators, that the music is going to stop,” one insurance actuary told the publication.

sentences.en: Granato and Drall estimate in their paper that private credit loan default rates above 15 percent could generate insolvency.
sentences.zh: Granato 和 Drall 在论文中估计，私人信用贷款违约率超过 15% 可能会导致破产。

sentences.en: The subscription-based Capitol Forum noted last week that KKR and Apollo’s three life insurers have just a tiny amount of room in its hardest-to-value assets to absorb losses.
sentences.zh: 基于订阅的 Capitol Forum 上周指出，KKR 和 Apollo 的三个人寿保险公司在其最难估值的资产中只有很小的空间来吸收损失。

sentences.en: “There is an expectation, even by the regulators, that the music is going to stop,” one insurance actuary told the publication.
sentences.zh: 一位保险精算师告诉该刊物：“即使是监管机构也预计音乐将会停止。”

blocks.html_en: A major life insurer insolvency is uncharted territory. “We’ve been very lucky, I think, that there’s been no major insurer insolvencies that have had to be mediated through the guaranty fund system, because there’s kind of an open question as to if this is even logistically possible to do,” Granato said. He noted that AIG, the insurer that collapsed after the 2008 crisis, was saved by quick action by the Fed and later Congress. “If AIG had been allowed to go under and then we would have had to manage 50 simultaneous AIG insolvencies across every state, in the middle of the financial crisis?” he asked. “You can imagine what a nightmare that would be.”

sentences.en: A major life insurer insolvency is uncharted territory.
sentences.zh: 大型人寿保险公司破产是一个未知领域。

sentences.en: “We’ve been very lucky, I think, that there’s been no major insurer insolvencies that have had to be mediated through the guaranty fund system, because there’s kind of an open question as to if this is even logistically possible to do,” Granato said.
sentences.zh: 格拉纳托说：“我认为，我们非常幸运，没有出现必须通过担保基金系统进行调解的重大保险公司破产事件，因为这在逻辑上是否可行，这是一个悬而未决的问题。”

sentences.en: He noted that AIG, the insurer that collapsed after the 2008 crisis, was saved by quick action by the Fed and later Congress.
sentences.zh: 他指出，美国国际集团（AIG）是一家在 2008 年危机后倒闭的保险公司，但美联储和后来的国会迅速采取行动，挽救了该公司。

sentences.en: “If AIG had been allowed to go under and then we would have had to manage 50 simultaneous AIG insolvencies across every state, in the middle of the financial crisis?”
sentences.zh: “如果允许 AIG 倒闭，那么在金融危机期间，我们就必须在每个州同时管理 50 家 AIG 破产案？”

sentences.en: he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问道。

sentences.en: “You can imagine what a nightmare that would be.”
sentences.zh: “你可以想象那将是一场多么可怕的噩梦。”

blocks.html_en: It’s unclear to Granato and Drall how we even ended up with this state guaranty/tax credit system; the historical literature shows shockingly little debate. But while protecting policyholders from ruin if their insurers made bad investments is certainly a good goal, doing it with after-the-fact assessments that get paid out by state tax credits is just a backdoor bailout. And it isn’t a particularly good disciplinary tool for the industry, as the insolvent insurer is off the hook from paying anything.

sentences.en: It’s unclear to Granato and Drall how we even ended up with this state guaranty/tax credit system; the historical literature shows shockingly little debate.
sentences.zh: 格拉纳托和德拉尔不清楚我们是如何最终建立这种国家担保/税收抵免制度的；历史文献中几乎没有争论。

sentences.en: But while protecting policyholders from ruin if their insurers made bad investments is certainly a good goal, doing it with after-the-fact assessments that get paid out by state tax credits is just a backdoor bailout.
sentences.zh: 但是，虽然在保险公司做出不良投资时保护保单持有人免遭破产无疑是一个好目标，但通过州税收抵免支付的事后评估只是一种后门救助。

sentences.en: And it isn’t a particularly good disciplinary tool for the industry, as the insolvent insurer is off the hook from paying anything.
sentences.zh: 对于该行业来说，这并不是一个特别好的纪律工具，因为资不抵债的保险公司无需支付任何费用。

blocks.html_en: “It makes sense if you had a good supervisory regime,” Drall said. But the weak regime means that risk-taking is incentivized, especially if a private equity fund can extract from the insurer along the way and be held harmless afterward.

sentences.en: “It makes sense if you had a good supervisory regime,” Drall said.
sentences.zh: “如果有一个良好的监督制度，那就有意义了，”德拉尔说。

sentences.en: But the weak regime means that risk-taking is incentivized, especially if a private equity fund can extract from the insurer along the way and be held harmless afterward.
sentences.zh: 但薄弱的制度意味着冒险行为受到激励，特别是如果私募股权基金能够一路从保险公司手中提取资金并在事后免受损害的话。

blocks.html_en: And when you bring in the fact that private credit is making all these data center loans, this risk-taking is dangerously concentrated. “Based on the fact that private equity firms specialize in this kind of lending, just the whole financial system is more and more aligned on that kind of activity,” said Drall. “And the more you do that, you know, AI better work out to sort of support the ecosystem.”

sentences.en: And when you bring in the fact that private credit is making all these data center loans, this risk-taking is dangerously concentrated.
sentences.zh: 当你考虑到私人信贷正在发放所有这些数据中心贷款的事实时，这种冒险行为就集中到了危险的程度。

sentences.en: “Based on the fact that private equity firms specialize in this kind of lending, just the whole financial system is more and more aligned on that kind of activity,” said Drall.
sentences.zh: 德拉尔表示：“基于私募股权公司专门从事此类贷款的事实，整个金融体系越来越与此类活动保持一致。”

sentences.en: “And the more you do that, you know, AI better work out to sort of support the ecosystem.”
sentences.zh: “你知道，你做得越多，人工智能就能更好地支持生态系统。”

blocks.html_en: Granato and Drall offer several reform proposals, mostly around making risks more transparent by reforming the valuation of private credit (including penalizing the companies for their opacity and complexity) and scrutinizing the rating agencies that claim the assets are safe. Internal transactions between private credit and the life insurer should have enhanced review, they argue, and the fees private equity takes out of the insurer should be identified in risk review.

sentences.en: Granato and Drall offer several reform proposals, mostly around making risks more transparent by reforming the valuation of private credit (including penalizing the companies for their opacity and complexity) and scrutinizing the rating agencies that claim the assets are safe.
sentences.zh: 格拉纳托和德拉尔提出了几项改革建议，主要是通过改革私人信贷的估值（包括惩罚不透明和复杂的公司）和审查声称资产安全的评级机构来提高风险透明度。

sentences.en: Internal transactions between private credit and the life insurer should have enhanced review, they argue, and the fees private equity takes out of the insurer should be identified in risk review.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，私人信贷和人寿保险公司之间的内部交易应该加强审查，私募股权从保险公司收取的费用应该在风险审查中确定。

blocks.html_en: But their big ask is to change how guaranty funds assess the industry after the fact instead of before, and how the tax credits effectively put the risk on taxpayers. An alternative would be assessing all companies before the fact, and assessing their corporate parents—including the private equity firms. “The core problem is having the ex post design in the first place, rather than funding it the way federal deposit insurance does it,” Granato said.

sentences.en: But their big ask is to change how guaranty funds assess the industry after the fact instead of before, and how the tax credits effectively put the risk on taxpayers.
sentences.zh: 但他们最大的要求是改变担保基金在事后而不是事前评估该行业的方式，以及税收抵免如何有效地将风险转嫁给纳税人。

sentences.en: An alternative would be assessing all companies before the fact, and assessing their corporate parents—including the private equity firms.
sentences.zh: 另一种选择是在事前评估所有公司，并评估其母公司——包括私募股权公司。

sentences.en: “The core problem is having the ex post design in the first place, rather than funding it the way federal deposit insurance does it,” Granato said.
sentences.zh: “核心问题是首先要进行事后设计，而不是像联邦存款保险那样为其提供资金，”格拉纳托说。

blocks.html_en: Otherwise, there’s this whole super-important industry that’s precariously tied to the AI bubble, and if the bet fails, we’d all be stuck holding the bag.

sentences.en: Otherwise, there’s this whole super-important industry that’s precariously tied to the AI bubble, and if the bet fails, we’d all be stuck holding the bag.
sentences.zh: 否则，整个超级重要的行业都与人工智能泡沫紧密相连，如果赌注失败，我们都将陷入困境。

content_html_zh:
一家在鼎盛时期价值 450 亿美元的对冲基金上周将其几乎全部股票投资组合出售给了 Citadel 证券。 就在一个月前，该基金的创始人、24 岁的前 OpenAI 员工利奥波德·阿申布伦纳 (Leopold Aschenbrenner) 在一封投资者信中表示，该基金今年的涨幅为 439%。 但其积极投资于人工智能行业相关公司的投资组合在 7 月份下降了 67%。

有趣的是，该基金被称为“态势感知”。

上周，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数出现了今年的第二次调整，该指数较峰值下跌了至少 10%。 自 6 月份 IPO 后的高点以来，SpaceX 的市值已相当于特斯拉的全部市值，而且仍在下跌。 无论出于什么原因——更便宜、更灵活的中国人工智能模型的崛起，美国人工智能公司根本没有产生足够的收入来证明资本支出飙升的合理性，特朗普关税和战争对整体经济的拖累，或者为保持车轮运转而采取的日益操作性的金融策略——对投资者来说，人工智能的光芒已经远去。

大卫·戴恩的更多作品

问题在于，该行业与股市的联系如此紧密，以至于人工智能投资者的感受发生变化可能会导致整个市场的崩溃，正如我们在某种程度上所看到的那样。 换句话说，如果人工智能在支撑经济，那么谁在支撑人工智能？

从一篇关于私人信贷和人寿保险行业的引人入胜的新论文中推断出的答案可能是美国纳税人。

私人信贷是私募股权公司 3 万亿美元的融资部门。 他们提供的贷款基本上不受监管、风险相对较高、相对复杂且不透明，而且大部分发放给自己的投资组合公司。 私人信贷可能比华尔街其他行业更陷入人工智能狂热之中。 例如，在 2010 年代中期，私募股权公司收购了数百家软件即服务提供商，其私人信贷附属机构向他们提供了数千笔贷款，但最近随着人工智能复制其任务，这些投资组合公司却陷入困境。

资不抵债的人寿保险公司不会破产，而是由国家担保基金支付其所有负债，特别是保单持有人的索赔。

私人信贷公司为在全国范围内建设人工智能数据中心而提供的所有贷款可以看到更深层次的交织。 随着建设延误的加剧——大约 530 个地方司法管辖区和计数已经通过了数据中心限制或禁令——而且人工智能行业似乎不太可靠，这些贷款可能会陷入大规模违约。 由于伊朗灾难性战争导致通货膨胀率居高不下，利率上升也成为私人信贷压力点。 因此，紧张的投资者的赎回请求继续增加。

然而，尽管股价暴跌，这一切都未能阻止私人信贷巨头的脚步。 KKR 是最大的公司之一，最近公布了创纪录的盈利。 如何解释这种脱节？ 它可能与一个独立的业务线有关，该业务线为许多私募股权公司提供了咨询巨头麦肯锡所描述的“永久资本”。

如今，私募股权公司在人寿保险公司中拥有至少 1.5 万亿美元的资产。 阿波罗于 2022 年收购了雅典娜； KKR 几年前收购了 Global Atlantic。 正如德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校助理教授 Andrew Granato 和博士 Pranjal Drall 在一篇研究论文中所解释的那样。 耶鲁大学的候选人表示，这些人寿保险公司拥有大量来自保单持有人付款的可用资本，这些资本在他们生命结束之前都不需要支付。 私募股权公司已将这些资金投入高风险的私人信贷贷款，这可能会削弱寿险公司的结构。 但如果保险公司资不抵债，私募股权公司就不必支付；你会。

这是因为，资不抵债的人寿保险公司不会破产，而是由国家担保基金支付其所有负债，特别是保单持有人的索赔。 事后，这些基金会对特定州幸存的人寿保险公司进行评估。 明显的想法是保护人寿保险受益人，并通过整个行业的费用来支付费用。 但政策设计的选择意味着成功的公司要为无力偿债的公司的不良行为付出代价。 在美国大部分地区，情况变得更糟：在 44 个州，人寿保险公司可以获得该评估的税收抵免，并在一段时间内获得 100% 的偿还。

换句话说，私人信贷公司承担的风险最终转移给了国家纳税人。 这是一个熟悉的利润私有化和风险社会化的故事。 私募股权公司早就嗅到了这个机会。

“这些鼓励保险公司承担如此大风险的激励措施已经存在很长时间了，”格拉纳托在接受采访时表示。 “但私募股权进入该业务标志着其资产负债表的资产管理状况发生了真正的急剧转变。” 私募股权正在利用救助担保计划，在非常接近边缘的情况下发挥作用，并威胁到整个经济。

私募股权公司从其与人寿保险公司的关系中获益匪浅。 格拉纳托和德拉尔发现，一家人寿保险公司被私募股权公司收购后，通常会将其内部投资团队削减一半，并在三分之一的情况下完全放弃该团队。 相反，人寿保险公司向私募股权公司的附属公司付费，让其为其投资。 会计、数据系统和其他服务的许多其他费用都集中到私募股权母公司身上。

人寿保险资本总是用于购买表现不佳的私人信贷贷款，而不是通常构成投资的国债和公司债券的无聊组合。 Granato 和 Prall 写道：“到 2024 年，新成立的私募股权保险公司的投资中有 49.5% 投资于私募工具。” 对于非附属人寿保险公司来说，这个数字约为 14%。

换句话说，自保人寿保险公司正在向其私募股权所有者泄露更多资金，并在其资产负债表上承担更高的风险。 没有保单持有人真正知道这种情况正在发生，也不习惯检查其人寿保险公司的资产。 德拉尔表示：“消费者实际上可能会得到更好的价格。”他指出，较高的风险往往伴随着较高的回报，至少在最初是这样。 “你可能会想象消费者甚至很乐意购买 Athene。”

当然，威胁在于所有这些不良私人信用贷款都被转入系统中不受客户或监管机构密切监控的部分。

保险产品在州一级由实力雄厚且经常被俘虏的保险专员进行监管。 他们没有专业知识来理解人寿保险公司收到的复杂贷款，而且他们也不想知道。 “最终发生的情况是，各州监管机构实际上正在相互竞争，以放松人寿保险监管，”格拉纳托说。 此外，私募股权公司还向宽松的评级机构支付费用，让其不良贷款获得良好的健康证明，这一点很快就得到了保险专员的认可。

Granato 和 Drall 在论文中估计，私人信用贷款违约率超过 15% 可能会导致破产。 基于订阅的 Capitol Forum 上周指出，KKR 和 Apollo 的三个人寿保险公司在其最难估值的资产中只有很小的空间来吸收损失。 一位保险精算师告诉该刊物：“即使是监管机构也预计音乐将会停止。”

大型人寿保险公司破产是一个未知领域。 格拉纳托说：“我认为，我们非常幸运，没有出现必须通过担保基金系统进行调解的重大保险公司破产事件，因为这在逻辑上是否可行，这是一个悬而未决的问题。” 他指出，美国国际集团（AIG）是一家在 2008 年危机后倒闭的保险公司，但美联储和后来的国会迅速采取行动，挽救了该公司。 “如果允许 AIG 倒闭，那么在金融危机期间，我们就必须在每个州同时管理 50 家 AIG 破产案？” 他问道。 “你可以想象那将是一场多么可怕的噩梦。”

格拉纳托和德拉尔不清楚我们是如何最终建立这种国家担保/税收抵免制度的；历史文献中几乎没有争论。 但是，虽然在保险公司做出不良投资时保护保单持有人免遭破产无疑是一个好目标，但通过州税收抵免支付的事后评估只是一种后门救助。 对于该行业来说，这并不是一个特别好的纪律工具，因为资不抵债的保险公司无需支付任何费用。

“如果有一个良好的监督制度，那就有意义了，”德拉尔说。 但薄弱的制度意味着冒险行为受到激励，特别是如果私募股权基金能够一路从保险公司手中提取资金并在事后免受损害的话。

当你考虑到私人信贷正在发放所有这些数据中心贷款的事实时，这种冒险行为就集中到了危险的程度。 德拉尔表示：“基于私募股权公司专门从事此类贷款的事实，整个金融体系越来越与此类活动保持一致。” “你知道，你做得越多，人工智能就能更好地支持生态系统。”

格拉纳托和德拉尔提出了几项改革建议，主要是通过改革私人信贷的估值（包括惩罚不透明和复杂的公司）和审查声称资产安全的评级机构来提高风险透明度。 他们认为，私人信贷和人寿保险公司之间的内部交易应该加强审查，私募股权从保险公司收取的费用应该在风险审查中确定。

但他们最大的要求是改变担保基金在事后而不是事前评估该行业的方式，以及税收抵免如何有效地将风险转嫁给纳税人。 另一种选择是在事前评估所有公司，并评估其母公司——包括私募股权公司。 “核心问题是首先要进行事后设计，而不是像联邦存款保险那样为其提供资金，”格拉纳托说。

否则，整个超级重要的行业都与人工智能泡沫紧密相连，如果赌注失败，我们都将陷入困境。
